slides.texte_overlay:
How to become extremely good
at first dates in your 20s
Suggest something with a natural ending. A coffee, a walk, a gallery. If it goes great, extend it. If not, nobody's trapped. Low pressure makes both of you more relaxed from the start.
Arrive five minutes early and pick a good spot. Not by the door, not under a speaker. A quiet corner where you can hear each other. It shows you thought about her comfort, not just yours.
Ask about her favorites. Favorite place she's travelled, favorite meal, favorite way to spend a Sunday. Favorites make people light up, and they tell you more than any job question.
Share a small story where you look a bit silly. The time you got lost in Rome or burned the pasta. A guy who can laugh at himself feels safe and fun to be around.
Keep your phone in your pocket and your attention on her. No checking the score, no glancing at messages. Full attention is rare, and it's the most attractive thing you can bring.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Every first date gets easier when you've always got a fun story ready to share.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Every first date gets easier when you've always got a fun story ready.

slides.texte_overlay: End with a clear, kind message. "I had a really good time, I'd love to see you again." No games, no waiting three days. Clear and kind is the best way to finish a first date.
